reels.title: A day on Venus is longer than its year
reels.hook: One spin of Venus takes longer than its whole trip around the Sun.
reels.caption:
A day on Venus is longer than its year. 🪐

Venus turns so slowly that one spin on its axis takes about 243 Earth days. One trip around the Sun takes only about 225.

And it spins backwards. If you could see through its thick clouds, you'd watch the Sun rise in the west and set in the east.

Which fact got you: the day or the sunrise? 👇

Follow for more facts that sound fake but aren't.

Source: NASA Science, Venus facts.

reels.title: You've never seen the Sun as it is right now
reels.hook: Sunlight takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach you, and Andromeda's light left before our species existed.
reels.caption:
You've never seen the Sun as it is right now. ☀️

Its light takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach you, so you always see it a little in the past. The farther you look, the older the light.

The Andromeda galaxy is visible to the naked eye from a dark site, and its light left about 2.5 million years ago. Our species has been around for roughly 300,000 years.

Would you rather see the Sun live or Andromeda as it is today? 👇

Sources: Smithsonian (How Things Fly), NASA Hubble (M31), Smithsonian Human Origins.
reels.alt_text: A 3D animation: the blazing Sun, a pulse of light racing to a small Earth, a pull-back through the stars to the Andromeda galaxy, then a night horizon under the sky. Bold captions read "The Sun · 8 min ago", "8 min 20 s late", "Farther = older", "2.5 million years" and "Before humans existed".

reels.title: A ball of iron under your feet as hot as the Sun
reels.hook: Earth's centre is about 6,000 °C, as hot as the Sun's surface, and pressure keeps it solid.
reels.caption:
There's a ball of iron under your feet as hot as the surface of the Sun. 🌍🔥

In 2013, researchers in Grenoble squeezed iron between two diamonds and found Earth's centre is about 6,000 °C (give or take 500). The Sun's surface is about 5,500 °C.

The pressure down there, over 3 million atmospheres, keeps that iron solid. The heat stirs the liquid iron around it, and that stirring makes the magnetic field your compass follows.

Which surprises you more: the heat or the pressure? 👇

Sources: ESRF (Anzellini et al., Science 2013), NASA Sun facts.
reels.alt_text: A 3D animation: Earth with a wedge cut away to show glowing layers and a white-hot inner core, a comparison with the Sun, then blue magnetic field lines looping around the planet. Bold captions read "As hot as the Sun", "~6,000 °C", "Sun's surface: 5,500 °C", "3+ million atmospheres" and "Heat makes the magnetic field".

reels.title: Saturn would float in water
reels.hook: Saturn is nine times wider than Earth, yet on average it's less dense than water.
reels.caption:
Saturn could float in a bathtub. 🪐🛁

It's about 9 times wider than Earth, but it's mostly hydrogen and helium, so its average density is less than water's.

That makes it the only planet in our solar system that would float, if you could find a tub big enough.

Which would you rather see: Saturn in a bathtub or Saturn up close? 👇

Follow for more facts that sound fake but aren't.

Source: NASA Science, Saturn facts.

reels.title: A sugar cube of neutron star
reels.hook: One sugar cube of neutron star material would weigh about a trillion kilograms.
reels.caption:
One sugar cube of neutron star material would weigh about a trillion kilograms. 🧊⭐

A neutron star is the crushed core left behind when a giant star dies. It packs around half a million Earths of mass into a ball only about 20 km across, roughly the size of a city.

What would you compare a trillion kilograms to? 👇

Source: NASA Goddard, Imagine the Universe: Neutron Stars.

reels.title: More trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way
reels.hook: About 3 trillion trees on Earth; 100 to 400 billion stars in our galaxy.
reels.caption:
Earth has more trees than the Milky Way has stars. 🌲✨

A global study in Nature estimated about 3.04 trillion trees. Our galaxy holds somewhere between 100 and 400 billion stars, so there are at least seven trees for every star.

And that count only includes trunks at least 10 cm wide.

Did you think it would be the other way round? 👇

Follow for more facts that sound fake but aren't.

Sources: Crowther et al., Nature (2015); ESA; NASA Goddard.

reels.title: Sink to the deepest point on Earth
reels.hook: Mount Everest would disappear underwater in the deepest part of the ocean.
reels.caption:
Mount Everest would disappear underwater in the deepest part of the ocean. 🌊

Sunlight fades by 200 m and is gone by 1,000 m. Most animals down there make their own light. Every night, trillions of them rise to feed: the biggest migration on Earth. The Titanic lies at 3,800 m; past 6,000 m is the hadal zone, named after Hades. The deepest fish ever filmed, a snailfish, was seen at 8,336 m in 2022. Researchers think that's near the limit for fish. Challenger Deep bottoms out around 10,935 m, at over 1,000 atmospheres. Two explorers first reached it in 1960 in the Trieste. Everest (8,849 m) would sit about 2 km under the surface.

Even there, a camera found a plastic bag (10,898 m). And less than a third of the seafloor has been mapped in detail.

Which stop surprised you most? 👇

Sources: NOAA Ocean Service, NOAA Ocean Exploration, MBARI (Martini & Haddock 2017), UWA (via NPR), Seabed 2030.
reels.alt_text: A 90-second animated dive from the ocean surface to Challenger Deep. A depth counter on the left climbs from 0 to 10,935 metres as sunlight fades, glowing creatures and marine snow drift past, a shipwreck and a whale appear, foam cups shrink under pressure, a snailfish and the Trieste bathyscaphe pass by, and a plastic bag rests on the trench floor. A cross-section shows Mount Everest sinking into the trench with about 2 kilometres of water above its peak.
